subject: Deployment mode follow-up: data isolation details requested
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@finorahealth.com>, Tom Keller <tom.keller@finorahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: deployment fit and data isolation follow-up

Hi Asha / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can align the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC / on‑prem):

What I heard
- You run a mix of PHI and aggregated analytics data for provider billing (primary concern: PHI controls, data residency).
- Security needs: customer-managed keys, strict audit logs, no co‑tenant access to model cache/state, and VPC peering restrictions.
- Procurement timeline: target decision by end of May; pilot in June.

Clarifying questions
1) Will any raw PHI (e.g., patient identifiers) be sent to model inputs, or will you only send tokenized/hashed identifiers? (This drives whether Hosted with BAA is sufficient vs requiring Private.)
2) Do you require hardware‑backed key storage (HSM) for KMS, or is KMS with CMKs acceptable?
3) Is on‑prem (air‑gapped) ever on the table, or do you prefer a cloud VPC-only approach?

Proposed next steps
- If you confirm PHI in payloads and mandatory HSM, we should scope Private (VPC or on‑prem) — I can loop in our infra lead for an architecture call.
- If PHI is tokenized and KMS with CMK is acceptable, Dedicated capacity inside a customer VPC will likely meet your needs with faster lead time.
- I attached a short SOC2 summary and our deployment options one‑pager.

Can you reply with answers to the three questions above and two preferred times for a 30‑minute technical call next week?

Thanks —
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, redwood-deployment-options-onepager.pdf

From: Asha Rao <asha@finorahealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Keller <tom.keller@finorahealth.com>, Finora Security <security@finorahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 12:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: deployment fit and data isolation follow-up

Logan —

Appreciate the recap. Quick answers inline: 

1) We will need to send PHI in the model inputs for the pilot (de‑identified in analytics flows but full PHI for clinical triage).
2) HSM-backed keys are strongly preferred; the security team will want proof of FIPS 140‑2 or compatible approach.
3) On‑prem is possible but not our first choice — a Private VPC with strict peering rules and customer‑managed KMS would be ideal given our cloud roadmap.

Next steps: please share a network/architecture diagram that shows how Dedicated differs from Private VPC (specifically around tenant isolation, KV cache handling, and management plane access). Also confirm whether Dedicated capacity can be combined with a customer‑managed KMS and isolated KV caches per tenant.

Availability: Tue 5/5 10:00–11:00 ET or Wed 5/6 14:00–15:00 ET for a technical call — Tom (cc'd) will join from infra.

Best,
Asha Rao
Head of Product Security | Finora Health

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@finorahealth.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: deployment fit and data isolation follow-up

Hi Asha —

Thanks for the quick answers — short technical points to prep for the call: 

- PHI in payloads: understood — we'll treat this as regulated workload.
- KMS/HSM: Redwood supports customer‑managed KMS keys in Dedicated and Private. For HSM attestation, we can present our keybroker options; on‑prem supports direct HSM integration (longer lead time).
- Tenant isolation & KV cache: Dedicated capacity provides tenant‑level process isolation and an option to run separate inference pools (no shared KV across pools). Private VPC (our preferred model for strict isolation) places the serving plane inside your VPC; management/control plane traffic is via an encrypted control channel, and we can restrict egress to your CIDR ranges.

I've uploaded a short network diagram and a one‑pager that outlines differences (see attachment and link). Also attaching a short checklist our compliance team typically needs for a Private VPC intake.

Attachments: redwood-network-diagram.pdf, redwood-deployment-options-onepager.pdf
Related link: https://redwood.app/drive/Finora-arch-diagram

Logan — can you own scheduling the technical call for Tue 5/5 10 ET? Ben, please stand by for procurement questions if they choose Private.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Asha Rao <asha@finorahealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Keller <tom.keller@finorahealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Finora Security <security@finorahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 15:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: deployment fit and data isolation follow-up

Monica / Logan —

Thanks — based on the diagram and the answers, we want to pursue Dedicated capacity inside a Private VPC topology (Dedicated pools + customer VPC where the serving plane resides). Critical asks before the technical call:

- Formal confirmation that KV cache is partitioned per customer (no cross‑tenant leakage) and a brief statement we can share with internal auditors.
- A short note on the KMS/HSM options with lead times and whether HSM‑backed CMKs can be brokered through our cloud KMS.
- Procurement pack (SLA, pricing ranges for Dedicated + Private VPC setup, and onboarding timeline).

If you can send those items ahead of Tue 5/5 10 ET, that will help our infra team prepare. We remain on for the 10:00 ET slot.

Asha Rao
Head of Product Security | Finora Health
